transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. Can you tell me what's been troubling you or what brings you in today?

Oh, hello Doctor. Thank you so much for seeing me today. I hope I'm not taking up too much of your valuable time. I want to be helpful, it's just... well, my family really wanted me to come in, and I want to do what's best. 

I've been terribly upset lately, and I'm so ashamed to even say this out loud to you because I know how awful it makes me look. I try so hard to be a good person, I really do. But... I keep telling my family that I’m the reason my friend passed away. I didn’t call her back when I should have, and... and I had some ugly thoughts sometimes. I feel so wicked for it. I just know the Lord is punishing everybody at our church because of me and the things I've done. 

I'm so sorry to lay all that on you right away... am I explaining things okay, Doctor? I just want to make sure I'm answering your question right.
Can you tell me more about these feelings of guilt and self-blame? How often do you feel this way, and does it affect your daily life?

Well, I... I feel it all the time, Doctor. From the moment I wake up until I finally manage to sleep. It's just this heavy, heavy weight. I hope I'm not sounding too dramatic. I know other people have real problems, and I shouldn't complain. 

As for my daily life... well, I try to keep up, I really do. But I have to admit, I've missed a few shifts at the store where I work as a cashier. And... well, I made a few mistakes on the register. Nothing malicious, I promise! Just... my mind was elsewhere, thinking about how wicked I've been. My supervisor noticed, and my niece got so worried about me. I felt terrible causing a fuss for them. 

And at home... oh, I'm so embarrassed to admit this. I've let some bills pile up on the counter. Unopened. It's not like me at all, I usually keep a very tidy house. I've also stopped going to my church groups and visiting the ladies. I just... I don't want to infect them with my badness, you know? They are such good people, and I don't deserve their company right now. 

Does that make sense, Doctor? I hope I'm giving you the right information. I just want to do whatever you think is best to fix me.
Have you had similar periods of feeling this way before, or is this the first time you’ve experienced these feelings of depression?

Well, Doctor... I, um... I've never felt quite this bad before. I mean, we all have our down days, don't we? I know I shouldn't make a mountain out of a molehill. I've always tried to be strong and keep a smile on my face for everyone else. 

But this... this heaviness, and these awful thoughts about what I've done... it's new. I've never felt so entirely wicked before, or like I was dragging other people down with my sins. I hope I'm not making it sound worse than it is, I really don't want to be a bother. Does that answer what you were asking, Doctor? I just want to make sure I'm giving you the right history.
Have you ever experienced periods where you felt unusually high, extremely energetic, or irritable, where you were doing or planning more things than usual, or where you needed less sleep?

Oh, no, Doctor. I... I don't think I've ever felt anything like that. I hope that's okay to say. I've always just been a rather quiet, ordinary sort of person, you know? Just going to work at the store and taking care of my home. 

I certainly haven't had any extra energy, and... well, I'd just hate to think I've ever been irritable or snapped at anyone. I try so hard to always be polite and kind to people, it would be just awful of me to act that way. As for sleep, I've always tried to get a proper night's rest. Well, until recently, of course, with all this awful guilt keeping me awake. But I've never felt like I actually needed less sleep, or had big plans or anything like that. 

Am I understanding your question correctly, Doctor? I really want to make sure I'm giving you the exact information you're looking for.

Have you found yourself having repeated, unwanted thoughts about doing something wrong or harmful, or felt driven to perform certain behaviors or mental acts to reduce the anxiety or guilt these thoughts cause?

Oh, goodness, no. I... I hope you don't think I would ever want to do anything harmful. I know I've been terribly wicked, like I said, but I don't have thoughts about... well, about hurting anyone or doing wrong things on purpose. I'd never want to cause any trouble like that, I promise. 

And I don't do any special habits or... or behaviors to make the guilt go away. I mostly just sit with it, because I know I deserve to feel this way. 

Does that make sense? I hope I'm answering your question the right way, Doctor. I just want to be absolutely sure I'm being helpful and giving you what you need.
Have you ever felt so low that you've thought about hurting yourself or that life wasn't worth living?

Well... oh, dear. I... I really don't want to worry you, Doctor. I know you're very busy and have so many other patients who are probably much worse off than I am. 

I mean... I wouldn't say I want to hurt myself, no. I'd never want to make a mess or cause a fuss for anyone else to have to clean up. But... well, sometimes, when the guilt is just so heavy and I think about all the awful things I've brought upon people... I do sometimes think that maybe... maybe everyone would just be better off if I wasn't here anymore. 

Just... just fading away quietly, you know? Not doing anything drastic. I'd never do that. Just... going to sleep and not waking up, so I couldn't be a burden or a wicked influence anymore. 

Is... is it alright that I said that? I'm so sorry if that's upsetting to hear. I just want to make sure I'm telling you the truth like you asked. Am I doing okay, Doctor?
Have you lost interest in activities you used to enjoy, like going to church or visiting with friends?

Well... oh, I suppose... I mean, I really don't want to sound like I'm complaining or being ungrateful for the life I have. I know I should be out doing things. 

But... well, yes. I used to just love going to choir practice, and my knitting circle... and playing bingo with the ladies. I even used to enjoy taking nice, long walks through Patterson Park. It was always so pretty. But lately... I don't know, Doctor. I just... I just sit in my chair at home. None of it really feels worth the trouble of getting dressed for anymore. I just can't seem to find the joy in it that I used to. 

I hope that doesn't make me sound lazy. I really do try to be a good, active person, I promise. I just... I just haven't had the heart for it lately. Is that the kind of thing you needed to know? I hope I'm explaining it right.
How long have you been feeling this way, Doctor? I want to make sure I understand if this has been going on for more than a few weeks or not.

Oh, well... let me think. I don't want to give you the wrong timeline and mess up your notes, Doctor. 

I suppose it's been... well, about two months now. Yes, right around two months. That's when my... my very dear friend passed away. It's been so hard without her, and I think that's when all this really started getting so heavy. I tried so hard to keep a stiff upper lip and not let it get to me, because I know she wouldn't want me moping around. But... it's just been about two months of feeling this way. 

I hope it's alright that it's been that long. I should have come to see you sooner, shouldn't I? I'm so sorry if I waited too long and made things difficult for you. Does two months sound like the right answer?
Have you ever had a period in your life where you felt unusually excited, overly confident, or full of energy for several days or more, where your mood was noticeably different from your usual self?

Oh, my... no, I don't think so. I hope that's not a bad thing. I've always just been a very steady, quiet sort of person... well, until all this happened, of course. 

I've never really been the type to get overly excited or, you know, burst with energy like that. I mostly just try to do my job at the register and keep my head down, not make a fuss. I'm so sorry if that's not the answer you were looking for. 

Is it... is it okay that I've never felt that way? I just want to be sure I'm giving you the right information, Doctor. I hope I'm not making your job harder by being so plain.
Have you noticed that your thoughts have been especially slow lately, or that it takes you longer than usual to process things or make decisions?

Well... oh dear. I really hate to admit this, because I know how important it is to be sharp, especially at my age. I don't want you to think my mind is going, Doctor. I really try to stay on top of things. 

But... yes, I suppose things have been a bit foggy lately. It's so embarrassing. At work... well, I've been a cashier for so long, you'd think I could do it in my sleep. But lately, I'll just stand there and stare at the register buttons like I've never seen them before in my life. It takes me a minute to remember what to push. And even at church, which I've gone to forever... the words in the hymnal just seem to blur together, and I completely lose my place. 

I try so hard to hide it so nobody worries, but it just takes me so much longer to figure things out right now. I hope that doesn't mean something terrible is wrong with me. Is it normal to get a little slow like that when you're feeling down? I hope I'm not being too much trouble by having so many things wrong with me.
Have you lost all interest in absolutely everything, to the point where nothing gives you pleasure anymore—not even things you used to enjoy, like seeing loved ones or your favorite activities?

Oh, goodness... I don't want to sound like I'm complaining or being ungrateful for the life I have, Doctor. I really don't. I know I should be out and about, keeping busy... 

But... well, yes, I suppose I have. It's awful to say it out loud. I used to just love my choir practice, and the knitting circle on Tuesdays, and our Thursday bingo games. I even used to enjoy taking a nice stroll through Patterson Park when the weather was fair. But lately... I just sit in my chair at home. None of it even feels worth getting dressed for anymore. 

I'm so sorry, I know that sounds terrible and lazy of me. I really should be trying harder to get out, shouldn't I? I hope you don't think poorly of me for letting myself go like this. Is it... is it common for people to lose their spark like that? I just want to make sure I'm giving you the right picture of what's happening.
